title: Yee FDTD and transient Maxwell finite elements

items.title: Stokes identity on a rectangular Yee face
items.strategy: Write the four oriented boundary integrals and use the one-dimensional fundamental theorem in each coordinate to obtain the face curl integral, with cyclic coordinate cases.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 2 §2.7, printed pp. 19–21: Stokes’ theorem and its use for electromagnetic curl equations. The coordinate-rectangle identity is verified locally.

items.title: Transient Maxwell system with piecewise materials and boundary conditions
items.strategy: State the real-field first-order Maxwell system, weighted energy spaces, charge continuity, PEC and periodic boundaries, and distributional interface convention without differentiating discontinuous coefficients.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.8–2.14, printed pp. 21–26: electric and magnetic boundary conditions, conductivity, PEC, and the time-varying Maxwell equations.

items.title: Oriented Maxwell cochains, masses, and the Yee grid
items.strategy: Define vertex, edge, face, and cell arrays, oriented incidence operators, positive material mass matrices, PEC relative and periodic closures, and the lossless and midpoint-conductive Yee leapfrog rows.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 3 §§3.2–3.3, printed pp. 30–36, and Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 246–249: Yee staggering and three-dimensional update rows.

items.title: Incidence curl has zero discrete divergence and gradient curl
items.strategy: Prove the two incidence compositions vanish by expanding oriented simplex/cubical boundaries and cancelling each codimension-two face with opposite signs, including PEC-relative and periodic identifications.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 8
references.locator: §8.3, printed pp. 170–172: oriented simplex degrees of freedom and the discrete de Rham incidence sequence.

items.title: The midpoint-conductivity Yee electric solve is well defined
items.strategy: Show the electric step matrix is symmetric positive definite when the permittivity mass is positive definite and conductivity is positive semidefinite.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.12, printed pp. 64–72, and Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 246–249: centered-in-time conductivity terms in staggered field updates.

items.title: Edge-face Maxwell finite element semidiscretization
items.strategy: Use lowest-order Nedelec edge and RT0 face spaces, their oriented discrete curl, exact coefficient-weighted mass matrices, the PEC boundary subcomplex, and the corresponding first-order and second-order transient equations.

references.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§1.1–1.2, printed pp. 1–5: lowest-order Nedelec edge fields, RT0 face fields, edge and face moments, and the curl commuting identity.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Richard S. Falk, and Ragnar Winther, Finite element exterior calculus: from Hodge theory to numerical stability
references.locator: §§5.1–5.3, printed pp. 49–53: Whitney finite element subcomplex, degrees of freedom, and lowest-order Nedelec/RT0 spaces.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron with a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh $\mathcal T_h$, and use the real lowest-order spaces $W_h^0,N_h^1,N_h^2,N_h^3$ defined in [[def-na-lowest-order-whitney-de-rham-spaces]]. The electric trial field is $E_h(t)\in N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$; the magnetic flux field is $B_h(t)\in N_h^2$, with no imposed zero normal trace on $B_h$. PEC means the closure-defined zero tangential subspace from [[def-na-zero-tangential-hcurl]]. Periodic analogues use the periodic cell complex. Countable Choice is inherited from the H(div) and affine Piola space definitions in the suppliers; the finite matrix operations below use no additional choice.

Put $V_h:=N_h^1\cap H_0(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)$. Choose an edge basis $\{\phi_i\}_{i=1}^{N_e}$ of the electric trial space $V_h$ and a face basis $\{\psi_a\}_{a=1}^{N_f}$ of $N_h^2$, so $N_e=\dim V_h$ and $N_f=\dim N_h^2$. Define the symmetric mass matrices
$$ (M_e)_{ij}=\int_\Omega \phi_j^T\epsilon\phi_i\,dx,\qquad (M_b)_{ab}=\int_\Omega \psi_b^T\mu^{-1}\psi_a\,dx.$$
They are positive definite by the coefficient bounds in [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]] and linear independence of the finite element bases. Let $C$ and $D$ be the coefficient matrices, in these chosen bases, of the restricted map $\operatorname{curl}:V_h\to N_h^2$ and of $\operatorname{div}:N_h^2\to N_h^3$. The moment-commuting supplier gives $DC=0$ on the full spaces, hence also after restriction to $V_h$. Set $j_i(t)=\int_\Omega J_{\rm src}(t)\cdot\phi_i\,dx$, with $J_{\rm src}\in C([0,T];L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3))$. The lossless, conductivity-free semidiscretization with this source is
$$M_e\dot e-C^TM_b b=-j,\qquad \dot b+Ce=0.$$
This is a spatial Galerkin system only; no time integrator is included. The cochain convention and weak material-interface formulation come from the declared spaces and [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]]. Smooth interpolation and a uniformly bounded commuting projection are separate prerequisites for the later error estimate and are not asserted by this definition.

items.title: Lossless or midpoint-conductive Yee leapfrog update
items.strategy: Specify the input cochains, source and conductivity samples, staggered time indices, exact magnetic and electric update rows, and their admissibility conditions.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 3 §§3.2–3.3 and §3.12, printed pp. 30–36 and 64–72; Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 246–249: staggered Yee update and centered conductivity treatment.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness for the finite-dimensional Maxwell ODE
items.strategy: Construct the matrix-exponential Duhamel solution for continuous loads and prove uniqueness by differentiating the inverse homogeneous flow.

references.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 6–8: finite-dimensional edge-element Maxwell systems. The continuous-load ODE construction is reduced to the local matrix-ODE supplier.

items.title: Maxwell curl-energy Ritz projection
items.strategy: Define the unique finite-dimensional projection for the sum of the permittivity L2 form and permeability-weighted curl form.

references.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 6–8: curl-energy Maxwell variational forms and conforming edge-element spaces. The time-dependent Ritz projection below is defined locally.

references.title: Peter Monk, Mathematical and Numerical Analysis of Maxwell’s Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: Chapter 11, ‘Finite Element Methods for Maxwell’s Equations’, printed pp. 151–168: Maxwell energy norms, conforming edge spaces, and error estimates.

items.title: Smooth lowest-order Nedelec and RT0 interpolation estimate
items.strategy: On shape-regular affine tetrahedra, subtract constant local approximants, bound the edge and face moment coefficients, scale the fixed reference bases, and sum the local curl and field estimates.

references.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§1.1–1.3, printed pp. 1–6: lowest-order Nedelec and RT0 degrees of freedom, their commuting curl identity, and the first-order curl interpolation estimate.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Richard S. Falk, and Ragnar Winther, Finite element exterior calculus: from Hodge theory to numerical stability
references.locator: §§5.2–5.4, printed pp. 50–55: lowest-order Whitney spaces, geometric degrees of freedom, and the warning that canonical moments require smooth inputs.

items.title: Compatible discrete charge and magnetic divergence propagate
items.strategy: Apply the transpose incidence identities to Ampere and the divergence incidence to Faraday, then use the stated discrete charge-continuity equation.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.2, printed pp. 30–31, and Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 246–249: staggered Maxwell updates and oriented Yee-grid placement. The discrete continuity proof below is local.

items.title: Strict spectral CFL positivity and Yee modified energy
items.strategy: Derive the exact staggered cross-energy identity, rewrite it using midpoint fields, and bound its negative curl term by the largest generalized curl-curl eigenvalue; treat equality separately.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 7 §7.4, printed pp. 164–168, and Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 246–249: FDTD dispersion relation, staggered field placement, and centered updates.

items.title: Second-order consistency of the homogeneous periodic Yee scheme
items.strategy: Use exact staggered central-difference formulas and Taylor remainders to bound the spatial curl-curl and centered time residual for smooth constant-coefficient periodic fields.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 246–249: 3D Yee staggering and update rows; Chapter 7 §7.4, printed pp. 164–168: central-difference dispersion. The truncation bound below is derived locally.

items.title: Semidiscrete edge-face Maxwell energy conservation
items.strategy: Differentiate the coefficient-weighted electric and magnetic quadratic energies and cancel the transposed discrete-curl pair.

references.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 6–8: the coefficient-weighted Maxwell curl-curl variational pairing and edge-element mass matrices. The semidiscrete first-order energy identity is proved locally.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 2 §2.14 and Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 25–26 and 246–249: Maxwell field energy convention and staggered curl exchange.

items.title: Well-definedness and best approximation of the Maxwell Ritz map
items.strategy: Prove coercivity, uniqueness and orthogonality of the finite-dimensional variational projection, then derive its best-approximation estimate.

references.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §2, printed pp. 6–8: the curl-energy Maxwell bilinear form; existence and orthogonality of the finite-dimensional projection are established locally.

items.title: Cartesian Yee symbol, numerical dispersion, and grid CFL bound
items.strategy: Compute the staggered Fourier symbol, identify longitudinal and transverse modes, derive the discrete plane-wave dispersion relation, and maximize the symbol for rectangular and cubic grids.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 7 §7.4, printed pp. 164–168, derives the 1D dispersion relation; Chapter 9 §§9.3 and 9.7, printed pp. 246–249 and 281–286, fixes the 3D Yee locations and unequal-step notation. The 3D symbol and maximum are derived locally.

items.title: Finite-time Yee error for smooth homogeneous periodic Maxwell fields
items.strategy: Apply the forced modified-energy identity to the sampled-solution residual and sum the energy increments under a strict CFL margin, with compatible exact starting rows.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 7 §7.4, printed pp. 164–168, gives the second-order dispersive relation; Chapter 9 §9.3 gives the 3D update. The finite-time residual-to-error estimate is proved locally.

items.title: Midpoint conductivity dissipates the Yee discrete energy
items.strategy: Take the material inner products of both staggered rows and show the curl exchanges cancel while the midpoint current contributes nonpositive work.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.12, printed pp. 64–72, Chapter 5 §5.7, printed pp. 129–133, and Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 246–249: conductivity update using a time-centered loss term.

items.title: Compatible magnetic initial projection for the Maxwell edge method
items.strategy: Correct the bounded commuting projection by its magnetic-mass orthogonal projection onto the discrete curl range; prove divergence preservation, curl orthogonality, and the smooth O(h) bound.

references.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§1.1–1.3, printed pp. 1–6: RT0 face-flux degrees of freedom, commuting divergence moments, and smooth-input interpolation estimates; the compatible projection below is constructed locally.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Richard S. Falk, and Ragnar Winther, Finite element exterior calculus: from Hodge theory to numerical stability
references.locator: §§3.3 and 5.2–5.5, printed pp. 22–24 and 50–57: bounded cochain projections, lowest-order Whitney spaces, and the stated limits of the projection outline.

items.title: Smooth PEC edge finite element Maxwell error from compatible projections
items.strategy: Assume sigma=0 (lossless branch); Use the PE09 cochain projection for compatible initial fields and divergence constraints, a local smooth interpolation estimate for O(h) approximation, and the Maxwell Ritz projection plus the semidiscrete energy identity for finite-time error.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a bounded contractible Lipschitz polyhedron with a shape-regular family of matching affine tetrahedral meshes, maximum diameter $h\to0$, and mesh-aligned material interfaces. Let $\epsilon,\mu$ be time-independent symmetric uniformly positive definite bounded coefficients. Let $(E,B)$ be a PEC solution of [[def-transient-maxwell-system-with-material-interfaces]] with $J_{\rm src}\in C^1([0,T];L^2(\Omega)^3)$, satisfying the stated current continuity and magnetic divergence constraints. Assume $E,E_t,E_{tt}$ are piecewise $C^1$ in space, their curls are piecewise $C^1$, and their tangential traces match across interior mesh faces and vanish on the exterior PEC boundary; assume $B(0)$ is piecewise $C^1$ with matching normal traces and $\operatorname{div}B(0)=0$. These bounds are uniform in time on $[0,T]$.

Take the semidiscrete solution of [[def-maxwell-edge-fem-semidiscretization]] with exact load moments, initialize $E_h(0)=R_hE(0)$ using the Maxwell Ritz map of [[def-maxwell-edge-ritz-projection]], and initialize $B_h(0)=B_h^0$ by [[lem-maxwell-magnetic-compatible-initial-projection]]. Write $\theta_h(t)=E_h(t)-R_hE(t)$. The Countable Choice assumption required by that projection interface is in force. Then the semidiscrete solution exists uniquely and
$$\sup_{0\le t\le T}\left(\|E_h(t)-E(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|\operatorname{curl}(E_h(t)-E(t))\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+\|B_h(t)-B(t)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\right)\le C_T h.$$
The constant depends on $T$, the coefficient bounds, the shape-regularity and projection bounds, and the stated piecewise smooth norms, but not on $h$. The initial magnetic projection preserves the discrete divergence constraint, and its error $B_h^0-B(0)$ is $\mu^{-1}$-orthogonal to all discrete curls. The result is a PEC semidiscrete estimate for smooth mesh-aligned data; it does not claim a rate across unresolved jumps or for nonsmooth fields.

references.title: Long Chen, Finite Element Methods for Maxwell Equations, complete lecture notes
references.locator: §§1.1–1.3, printed pp. 1–6: lowest-order edge and face spaces, commuting moments, and smooth interpolation estimates; the transient Ritz-energy argument is proved locally.

references.title: Douglas N. Arnold, Richard S. Falk, and Ragnar Winther, Finite element exterior calculus: from Hodge theory to numerical stability
references.locator: §§3.3 and 5.2–5.5, printed pp. 22–24 and 50–57: bounded cochain projections and lowest-order Whitney spaces; §5.5 is only an outline and is not treated as a completed proof.

title: Yee FDTD and transient Maxwell finite elements — Examples

items.title: A smooth Maxwell eigenmode in a rectangular PEC cavity
items.strategy: Construct an explicit divergence-free trigonometric field, verify all tangential PEC traces vanish, and compute its continuous frequency.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 8 §8.8, printed pp. 225–227: PEC boundary implementation; the rectangular cavity field is checked directly.

items.title: Normal-incidence reflection at a planar dielectric interface
items.strategy: Match tangential electric and magnetic traces at a planar interface and solve the resulting two scalar equations for reflection and transmission amplitudes.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 5 §5.8, printed pp. 133–135: plane-wave reflection and transmission at a material interface.

items.title: A current violating discrete continuity creates Gauss-law drift
items.strategy: Use an oriented periodic edge current with nonzero incidence divergence but a fixed charge row, then compute the first-step Gauss residual exactly.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 3 §3.2, printed pp. 30–31, and Chapter 9 §9.3, printed pp. 246–249: Yee source rows and discrete divergence behavior.

items.title: Periodic Yee plane-wave dispersion and the cubic CFL limit
items.strategy: Substitute a single transverse Fourier mode into the exact three-dimensional symbol and evaluate the axis and corner frequency relations.

references.title: John B. Schneider, Understanding the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method
references.locator: Chapter 7 §7.4, printed pp. 164–168: plane-wave Yee dispersion; the cubic three-dimensional corner calculation below is explicit.
